# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments (fictional)
**Program:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Client Profile Block v1.0 and discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with about 1,100 staff. The Client's AI maturity is recorded as Piloting. The Profile Block lists three AI use cases:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The regulatory drivers recorded are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The certification target is ISO/IEC 42001, with work to start next year. The start date is not fixed. The Profile Block records an internal audit finding from June 2026: no inventory of AI systems.

The stated objective, in Dana Whitfield's words, is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The Profile Block records three constraints:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

The incumbent frameworks listed are an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. The Client has not completed a prior Academy program. A decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at the Piloting Stage

At the Piloting stage, governance decisions are made alongside delivery decisions rather than after them. A pilot that moves toward production creates questions in a predictable order:

- What is in scope?
- Who is accountable?
- What evidence is needed?
- What oversight applies to people and processes affected by the system?

A one-time assessment answers these questions at a single point. Continuous fractional advisory keeps them answered as the pilot changes, as new use cases arrive and as certification work begins.

The engagement is grounded in three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. In practice, this means each AI system is understood and documented before it scales. Each deployment decision is made with its purpose and risks stated. Accountability stays with named people at the Client.

The program works from two open frameworks the Client keeps after the engagement ends:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Board-level reporting draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. The Annual Arc

The arc is sequenced so that governance for visual inspection is in place ahead of the stated Q2 2027 production target. ISO/IEC 42001 preparation intensifies in the second half of the year. The engagement start date is Unknown. Whether the first two program quarters fall before Q2 2027 depends on that date and will be confirmed at intake. The ISO/IEC 42001 audit date is Unknown and flagged for intake.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize.** The program will:

- Establish an AI system inventory covering the deployed, piloting and planned use cases, responding to the June 2026 internal audit finding.
- Draft a governance charter and an accountability map.
- Set intake criteria for new AI use cases using GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook).

Questions to confirm at intake:

- Does the customer data residency constraint apply to the chatbot?
- Does the works council consultation constraint apply to the visual inspection pilot?
- Which existing ISMS, quality management and internal audit processes, if any, the Client wishes to extend to AI governance.

**Quarter 2: Deepen.** The program will focus on the visual inspection pilot ahead of the production target:

- A use-case risk and impact assessment.
- Human oversight design.
- Production acceptance criteria.
- A documented go or no-go decision record, using Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen).

Where works council consultation applies, the program will support the Client in sequencing governance artifacts so they are available for that consultation. EU AI Act and GDPR questions arising from this work will be flagged for verification by counsel.

**Quarter 3: Assure.** The program will prepare for ISO/IEC 42001 readiness:

- A gap assessment against the standard.
- An evidence collection plan.
- A draft scope for the AI management system.
- Support for internal audit planning, as the Client chooses.

This work is readiness preparation. It does not predict any certification outcome.

**Quarter 4: Evolve.** The program will:

- Apply the intake criteria to the planned AI sales forecasting use case.
- Review the deployed chatbot against the matured governance artifacts.
- Assess progress toward ISO/IEC 42001 readiness.
- Prepare the Month 11 renewal and handover options.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

The engagement includes:

- **A monthly executive advisory session** focused on decisions, risks and regulatory developments.
- **A monthly working session** with the governance team on artifacts and implementation.
- **Asynchronous availability** for defined question categories, with response windows and escalation paths agreed in the first month.
- **A quarterly governance review** against the annual arc.

Attendance for each session will be confirmed at intake from the audience roles listed in the Profile Block:

- General Counsel
- CISO
- Head of Quality
- Head of Data
- German plant manager
- Two internal auditors

## 5. Scope

**In scope:** governance evolution, implementation guidance, audit preparation, AI strategy and executive decision support.

**Out of scope:** legal advice, certification body functions, staff augmentation and incident command.

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act and GDPR interpretation, route to external counsel. Regulatory developments raised during the engagement are flagged for counsel verification and are not presented as settled advice.

## 6. Investment

The program runs for twelve months, renewable, at US$10,000 per month. This is a twelve-month total of US$120,000.

The Profile Block records a budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. The Client's fiscal year boundaries are Unknown. The intake will confirm how the monthly fee falls across fiscal years and whether the budget for the following fiscal year requires a separate approval.
